questions.help:
FACTORS THAT AFFECT PHYSICAL CAPABILITIES
 
11.1 Causes of drowsiness
Less hours sleeping than normal. If an individual has stayed awake through part of the night, they will feel very sleepy the next day, especially if they’e slept less than half of the hours needed or normally taken. Sleeping two hours less each night in a few days will result in a strong feeling of drowsiness.
Changing sleep patterns. People who frequently change the periods and hours for sleeping (for example, shift workers) often go through periods of intense drowsiness when they are awake. Most noticeably this occurs at the time of the day when the individual would normally or most often be going to bed or just after this period.

19 The consequences of illnesses and drugs in traffic collisions
To drive a vehicle requires certain conditions relating to the physical and mental aptitude of the driver to be initially satisfied and thereafter maintained. It is therefore necessary to go to a designated medical centre for drivers who will verify whether there is a serious impediment to the applicant or driver, which will prevent them performing this task safely.
A mild illness does not have to exclude driving, although it can reduce the ability to drive safely (for example, a common cold can cause sleepiness and loss of concentration). 2.2 Signal: Advising and warning of the manoeuvre
The reversing light advises and warns that the vehicle is, or is about to, reverse back and that reverse gear has been selected. If an arm signal is used to convey this warning then the driver must extend his arm horizontally and turn the palm of his hand backwards.
(Página 183 del manual 'Learning to drive')

3 Circumstantial signalling, beaconing elements and vehicle restraint systems
 
3.2 Beaconing elements
3.2.2 Guiding devices
3.2.2.10 Longitudinal auditory guides
Small grooves in the pavement or raised markings that, when driven over, produce vibration and/or sound. Their purpose is to alert drivers to unintended deviations from the vehicle’s trajectory.
(Página 114 del manual 'Learning to drive')
